newsitem.title: USA: Dow index sets fourth straight record high.
newsitem.headline: Dow index sets fourth straight record high.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average powered into record territory for the fourth session in a row Monday as investors bet that interest rates will continue to fall, making stocks even more attractive.
The Dow ended up 35.78 points at 6,255.60, eclipsing Friday's record closing high of 6,219.82.

It was the Dow's fourth consecutive record closing high and the longest string of new milestones since the seven-session streak from Feb. 5 to 13. Last week's 198-point post-election rally was the second-biggest weekly point gain ever after the 207-point surge in the week of Aug. 2 this year.

In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,391 to 996 on moderate volume of 353 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange, where trading was somewhat muted due to the observance of Veterans' Day.

Other market gauges also set new highs. The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 1.05 to 731.87, its fifth consecutive record and the NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks gained 0.51 to 386.83, a new high.

The technology-studded Nasdaq Composite index rose 5.16 to 1,262.67, topping its Oct. 15 record of 1,258.10 on bullishness prior to release after the close of the Semiconductor Industry Association's book-to-bill report for October.
Stocks were bolstered by the prospect that the Federal Reserve will hold monetary policy steady at Wednesday's meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee.

The market also got a shot in the arm after Smith Barney raised the stock portion in its recommended asset allocation to 50 percent from 45 percent, cut cash to 10 percent from 15 percent and kept bonds at 40 percent.

Smith Barney's portfolio strategist, Marshall Acuff, said the firm's investment policy committee was motivated by a stronger bond market, as well as expectations that interest rates would not rise near-term, and the belief that overseas growth is expanding slowly enough not to pressure U.S. rates.
"We recognise the equity market has done well since July," he said. "But typically stocks don't go down in a positive monetary environment."
Acuff said the brokerage house still believes that the market's valuations are high.
"We're not suggesting everything is right with the world but typically bull markets end when the Fed tightens and we don't see that anytime soon," he said.

The stock of computer chip companies surged in anticipation that the closely watched book-to-bill ratio -- a measure of the industry's activity -- would top the 1.0 level for the first time this year.
It came in at 1.10, versus a revised 0.98 in September and the highest since December of 1995's 1.12 level.
A book-to-bill of 1.0 means that for every dollar of computer chips shipped, one dollar of new orders was recorded.
Intel was up 1-5/8 to 123-7/8, Micron rose 1-7/8 to 31-7/8 and Atmel added two to 30-7/8.
Among special situations, PHH Corp. jumped 17 to 47-3/4 after it agreed to merge with HFS Inc. in a $1.7 billion deal that values PHH at $49.50 a share. HFS lost 1-1/4 to 72-7/8.
Drug wholesaler Bergen Brunswig slumped 5-1/8 to 27-5/8 on news of its $1.65 billion merger with IVAX, a generic drug maker.

IVAX fell 3-3/8 to 12-3/8 on concern that Bergen's relationships with other distributors may be impaired as a result of the merger and that it is making a strategy shift with a company that is going through some problems.
Philip Morris rose 1-1/2 to 99-3/8 after the College Retirement Equities Fund rejected a resolution urging the sale of its tobacco-related holdings.

Globalstar Telecommunications rose 2-7/8 to 56-1/2. It reached an agreement with a unit of China's Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications to extend a global mobile satellite system to customers in China.
The American Stock Exchange index was off 0.66 points to 579.73. The average NYSE share was up 6 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at new high of 7,082.634 up 12.747 or 0.18 percent.
